headline: Federal High Court Remands Journalist Daniel Ojukwu In Abuja
seoTitle: Journalist Daniel Ojukwu Remanded In Abuja
metaDescription: A Federal High Court has ordered journalist Daniel Ojukwu to be held in Kuje Correctional Centre following charges related to cyberstalking reports.
aiSummaryBullets: Journalist Daniel Ojukwu was ordered to be remanded in Kuje Correctional Centre by a Federal High Court in Abuja.
The detention follows cyberstalking charges brought against the journalist regarding his reporting on a former presidential aide.
The court mandated that the journalist remain in custody until the next hearing scheduled for 1 December.
aiContextParagraph: The Federal High Court in Abuja has issued a remand order for journalist Daniel Ojukwu, who is affiliated with the Foundation for Investigative Journalism. The legal action stems from reports published in 2023 concerning a former aide to a former president. Ojukwu faces accusations of cyberstalking in relation to his investigative work. According to court proceedings, the journalist will be held at the Kuje Correctional Centre for a period of 21 days while the case continues. The next court session is currently set for the first day of December. This incident highlights ongoing discussions regarding the intersection of investigative journalism, legal definitions of cyberstalking, and the detention of media professionals in Nigeria. Official records confirm the detention order and the scheduled timeline for future proceedings as reported by local media outlets covering the legal developments in the capital city.
